title: Bungie 对 Marathon 进行大规模重做，偏离最初的撤离射击设计愿景
content:
Bungie overhauls Marathon from original extraction shooter vision
Business
PC
Console
News
Bungie is overhauling Marathon from its original extraction shooter vision
Bungie says addressing player feedback requires the team to 'change both what we're building and how we deliver it,'
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 15, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Bungie
After experimenting with a casual player versus player-lite (PvP) mode in June, Bungie is implementing a permanent PvE mode to
Marathon
, its frantic shooter, later in the year. At the same time, this is one of the ways in which the studio is overhauling its original vision for the game, amidst ongoing changes and pressure on the team.
In an
update shared yesterday
, Bungie said that it's delaying a September 22 update to December 8. Among some additions and tweaks, the update will include a permanent PvE experience called Symbiosis. The studio is calling the mode "the first major step" in
Marathon's
next chapter.
"The update will introduce
Marathon’s
first permanent PvE experience, providing a new way to explore, progress, and engage with the world beyond traditional PvPvE extraction gameplay," the announcement reads. "Symbiosis is an important milestone for
Marathon
and the beginning of a broader evolution through March and beyond, shaped by what we learn from players along the way."
Related:
Wardogs lead says the studio won't hire people who decry crunch on social media
At the same time, Bungie is moving away from a "strict seasonal schedule," with the goal of giving the team more flexibility to build and test features before they're released. These type of
overhauls
for online games can be technically and logistically complex on the best of days.
"Since launch, you've told us
Marathon
needs more depth, more variety, stronger progression, and better reasons to keep playing over the long term. We agree. Addressing that feedback requires us to change both what we’re building and how we deliver it," Bungie says.
These changes come during a tumultuous time for Bungie. In late June, parent company
Sony laid off at least 292 Bungie employees
, officially presented as "most" of the Destiny team and "some"
Marathon
developers. The news came a month after Bungie announced it was
ending live development on Destiny 2
.
At the time, Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Hermen Hulst spoke about
Marathon's
place under PlayStation. "
Marathon
remains an important part of our portfolio, and we will continue to support the team as they build on the strong foundation established in Season 1 and 2, and as they work on incubation efforts for future projects," Hulst said. "While it's too early to discuss, we are encouraged by the creativity and opportunities that lie ahead."
Now, Bungie is talking about the current changes to the game as a reset of sorts. The team is set to release a blog detailing more about future plans later this month, in which it will share how the team will be evolving
Marathon
into a "more alien and dynamic" experience.
Related:
Why does this prominent Washington state politician think video games can be 'soft power?'
"Symbiosis will be a significant milestone for
Marathon
, introducing permanent PvE and several new ways to engage with the game," yesterday's update reads. "But it’s only the beginning of what we're working toward. As players spend time with these updates and share their feedback, we’ll continue refining and expanding
Marathon
."
